red_flags.indicator: Mild wheeze, able to speak in sentences
red_flags.followup_question: Are you able to speak in full sentences despite the wheezing?

red_flags.indicator: No distress
red_flags.followup_question: Is your breathing otherwise comfortable?

red_flags.indicator: Large surface area or high-risk mechanism of injury
red_flags.followup_question: How large is the abraded area and how did the injury happen?

red_flags.indicator: Small, superficial, uncomplicated
red_flags.followup_question: Is it a small, superficial scrape?

ctas_level_guidance.5: Small, superficial (classified as an abrasion under moderate/minor bleeds).

source_pages: p.27-28 (Bleeding Disorder modifier - abrasions and superficial lacerations classified as moderate/minor bleeds)

red_flags.indicator: Deep bite with significant tissue loss, uncontrolled bleeding, or high-risk animal (rabies concern)
red_flags.followup_question: How deep is the bite, and was it from an animal that might carry rabies (e.g. bat, unknown/wild animal)?

red_flags.indicator: Minor bite with mild acute peripheral pain
red_flags.followup_question: Is this a minor bite without heavy bleeding?

ctas_level_guidance.5: Minor bites +/- mild acute peripheral pain (level 5 example in manual).

red_flags.indicator: High-risk exposure (e.g. known positive source, mucous membrane/deep percutaneous exposure)
red_flags.followup_question: Was the exposure to a known high-risk source, or a deep needlestick or mucous membrane splash?

red_flags.indicator: Low risk exposure
red_flags.followup_question: Was this a superficial or low-risk exposure?

ctas_level_guidance.3: Low risk exposure (Selected Special Complaints table).

red_flags.indicator: Burn >25% body surface area (BSA)
red_flags.followup_question: How much of your body surface is burned - would you estimate more or less than a quarter?

red_flags.indicator: Airway/inhalation involvement (facial burns, singed nasal hair, soot in airway)
red_flags.followup_question: Was your face involved, or did you breathe in smoke?

red_flags.indicator: Smaller area, no airway involvement
red_flags.followup_question: How large is the burned area and is your breathing normal?

ctas_level_guidance.2: Burn >25% BSA (Selected Special Complaints table), or airway involvement.

red_flags.indicator: Cyanosis with respiratory distress or altered LOC
red_flags.followup_question: Along with the blue color, are they having severe trouble breathing or are they less responsive?

ctas_level_guidance.1: Cyanosis is generally a sign of severe respiratory distress (CTAS 1 per Respiratory Distress table).

red_flags.indicator: Deep embedded object with neurovascular concern or signs of infection
red_flags.followup_question: Is the object deeply embedded, and is there any numbness or spreading redness?

red_flags.indicator: Superficial, minor
red_flags.followup_question: Is it a small, superficial object like a splinter?

red_flags.indicator: Uncontrolled bleeding or deep laceration (life/limb threatening bleed category)
red_flags.followup_question: Is the bleeding uncontrolled even with direct pressure?

red_flags.indicator: Sutures required, active but controlled bleeding - CTAS Level 4 case example (3cm laceration, no active bleeding, pain 4/10)
red_flags.followup_question: Is the bleeding controlled, and roughly how large and deep is the cut?

ctas_level_guidance.4: Laceration requiring sutures, controlled (manual case example: 3cm laceration, pain 4/10).

source_pages: p.19, 27-28, 55 (CTAS Level 4 case example, Bleeding Disorder modifier, Selected Special Complaints table)

red_flags.indicator: Rapidly spreading redness, severe pain out of proportion, fever, or dark/black skin discoloration (necrotizing fasciitis concern)
red_flags.followup_question: Is the redness spreading quickly, is the pain worse than expected, or is any skin turning dark?

red_flags.indicator: Localized, stable, no systemic signs
red_flags.followup_question: Is the swelling/redness staying in one area without spreading quickly?

red_flags.indicator: Rapid growth, pain, or systemic symptoms
red_flags.followup_question: Has this grown quickly or become painful?

red_flags.indicator: Chronic, stable, asymptomatic
red_flags.followup_question: Has this been stable and unchanged for a long time?

red_flags.indicator: Signs of systemic illness (fever, spreading, blistering of large body surface)
red_flags.followup_question: Do you have a fever, or is the skin condition spreading quickly or blistering?

red_flags.indicator: Localized, no systemic symptoms
red_flags.followup_question: Is this localized without fever or other symptoms?

red_flags.indicator: Associated with airway swelling or respiratory distress (anaphylaxis)
red_flags.followup_question: Along with the itching, is your throat or face swelling, or do you have trouble breathing?

red_flags.indicator: Widespread, distressing itch, no respiratory symptoms
red_flags.followup_question: Is the itching widespread and bothersome, without any breathing difficulty?

red_flags.indicator: Rash with airway swelling, tight throat, dizziness (anaphylaxis pattern)
red_flags.followup_question: Along with the rash, is your throat feeling tight or are you feeling dizzy?

red_flags.indicator: Rash with fever and looking unwell (concern for meningococcemia or other serious infection)
red_flags.followup_question: Do you have a fever, and does the rash look like small bruises or dark spots that don't fade with pressure?

red_flags.indicator: Widespread rash, well-appearing, no fever
red_flags.followup_question: Do you feel well otherwise, without fever?

red_flags.indicator: Fever with spreading redness (mastitis/abscess concern)
red_flags.followup_question: Do you have a fever along with the breast redness and tenderness?

red_flags.indicator: Mild, localized, no fever
red_flags.followup_question: Is it localized without fever?

red_flags.indicator: Signs of wound infection or dehiscence
red_flags.followup_question: Does the wound look infected, red, swollen, or is it coming apart?

red_flags.indicator: Routine, healing well
red_flags.followup_question: Is the wound healing well with no signs of infection?

red_flags.indicator: Widespread, severe itching, secondary skin infection
red_flags.followup_question: Is the itching severe, and does the skin look infected?

red_flags.indicator: Mild, no infection signs
red_flags.followup_question: Is this mild without signs of skin infection?

red_flags.indicator: Extensive bruising with bleeding disorder history or suspected internal bleeding
red_flags.followup_question: Do you have a bleeding disorder or take blood thinners, and is the bruising extensive or in unusual places?

red_flags.indicator: Limited, no bleeding disorder, stable
red_flags.followup_question: Is the bruising limited to a small area?

red_flags.indicator: Airway swelling, respiratory distress, or hemodynamic compromise (anaphylaxis)
red_flags.followup_question: Is your throat swelling or are you having severe trouble breathing after the sting?

red_flags.indicator: Localized swelling/pain only
red_flags.followup_question: Is the reaction limited to swelling and pain at the sting site?

red_flags.indicator: Signs of infection (spreading redness, fever, increased pain, pus)
red_flags.followup_question: Does the wound look infected - more red, swollen, or draining pus - or do you have a fever?

red_flags.indicator: Healing well, routine check
red_flags.followup_question: Is the wound healing as expected?

red_flags.indicator: Altered LOC (GCS<9), respiratory depression, or hemodynamic instability
red_flags.followup_question: Are they awake and breathing normally right now?

red_flags.indicator: Altered LOC (GCS 10-13) or ingestion of a potentially lethal substance/dose
red_flags.followup_question: What substance and how much was taken, and are they drowsy or confused?

red_flags.indicator: Alert, stable, low-risk ingestion
red_flags.followup_question: Are they fully alert, and was the ingestion a smaller or less dangerous amount?

red_flags.indicator: Altered LOC, respiratory depression, or aggressive/violent behaviour posing safety risk
red_flags.followup_question: Are they alert and cooperative, or drowsy, confused, or aggressive?

red_flags.indicator: Awake, cooperative, stable vital signs
red_flags.followup_question: Are they able to answer questions and walk safely?

source_pages: p.23-24, 58-59 (Hemodynamic/LOC modifiers, Mental Health safety-risk definitions applied)

red_flags.indicator: Seizure, hallucinations (delirium tremens), or significant hemodynamic instability
red_flags.followup_question: Have you had any seizures, hallucinations, or a racing heart along with the withdrawal symptoms?

red_flags.indicator: Moderate symptoms (tremor, anxiety, nausea), stable vitals
red_flags.followup_question: Are you shaky, anxious, or nauseated, but otherwise feeling stable?

red_flags.indicator: Mild symptoms
red_flags.followup_question: Would you describe your withdrawal symptoms as mild?

red_flags.indicator: Hemodynamic compromise / shock, or high-risk MOI (impact >40-60km/h, rollover, ejection)
red_flags.followup_question: Are you feeling faint, weak, or dizzy since the injury, and how fast was the impact?

red_flags.indicator: Bleeding disorder-relevant bleed location (abdomen classified as life/limb threatening bleed site)
red_flags.followup_question: Is there any significant pain in your abdomen, and do you have a bleeding disorder or take blood thinners?

red_flags.indicator: Stable, low-risk mechanism
red_flags.followup_question: Was this a lower-speed or lower-impact incident, and are you feeling stable?

ctas_level_guidance.2: High-risk MOI or abdominal bleed (life/limb threatening bleed site).

source_pages: p.23, 27-29 (Hemodynamic / Bleeding Disorder / MOI modifiers applied)

red_flags.indicator: Any penetrating injury to the abdomen (high-risk mechanism per manual's General Trauma MOI table)
red_flags.followup_question: Where exactly did the penetrating object enter, and is there heavy bleeding?

red_flags.indicator: Hemodynamic compromise / shock
red_flags.followup_question: Are you feeling faint or very weak?

ctas_level_guidance.2: Penetrating injury to torso is a high-risk mechanism of injury (CTAS 2 minimum).

source_pages: p.29 (Mechanism of Injury - General Trauma, penetrating injury to torso)

red_flags.indicator: Respiratory distress, hemodynamic compromise, or high-risk MOI
red_flags.followup_question: Are you having severe trouble breathing or feeling faint since the chest injury?

red_flags.indicator: Chest is a life/limb threatening bleed site under the Bleeding Disorder modifier
red_flags.followup_question: How severe is the chest pain, and how did the injury occur?

red_flags.indicator: Stable, minor injury
red_flags.followup_question: Is your breathing comfortable and the pain manageable?

ctas_level_guidance.2: Chest bleed site or high-risk MOI.

red_flags.indicator: Any penetrating chest injury (high-risk mechanism)
red_flags.followup_question: Where did the penetrating injury occur, and is there heavy bleeding or trouble breathing?

red_flags.indicator: Hemodynamic/respiratory compromise
red_flags.followup_question: Are you having severe difficulty breathing or feeling faint?

ctas_level_guidance.2: Penetrating injury to torso (high-risk MOI, CTAS 2 minimum).

source_pages: p.29 (Mechanism of Injury - General Trauma, penetrating injury to torso)

red_flags.indicator: Shock, in obvious distress with unstable vital signs
red_flags.followup_question: Are they showing obvious signs of distress with unstable vital signs?

red_flags.indicator: No obvious injury but pedestrian struck by vehicle travelling at speed - CTAS Level 2 case example
red_flags.followup_question: Was this a pedestrian struck by a fast-moving vehicle, even without obvious visible injury?

red_flags.indicator: Prolonged spinal immobilization required, otherwise stable
red_flags.followup_question: Are they currently immobilized on a spine board with no severe injuries identified yet?

ctas_level_guidance.2: High-energy mechanism, no obvious injury (manual case example: pedestrian struck at speed).
ctas_level_guidance.3: Prolonged spinal immobilization (Selected Special Complaints table).

source_pages: p.17-18, 55 (CTAS Level case examples, Selected Special Complaints table)

red_flags.indicator: Shock / major trauma with unstable vital signs
red_flags.followup_question: Are they showing signs of shock with unstable vital signs?

red_flags.indicator: Penetrating injury to torso, proximal extremities, or high-risk location
red_flags.followup_question: Where is the penetrating injury located?

ctas_level_guidance.2: Penetrating injury, high-risk location (Mechanism of Injury table).

source_pages: p.17, 29 (CTAS Level 1 definition, Mechanism of Injury modifier)

red_flags.indicator: Critical/panic value with symptomatic patient
red_flags.followup_question: Do you know which lab value was abnormal, and are you having any symptoms right now?

red_flags.indicator: Abnormal but stable, asymptomatic
red_flags.followup_question: Are you feeling well despite the abnormal result?

red_flags.indicator: Referral indicates urgent condition per referring provider
red_flags.followup_question: Did the referring provider indicate this needs to be seen urgently?

red_flags.indicator: Routine, non-urgent referral
red_flags.followup_question: Is this a routine referral without urgent concerns noted?

red_flags.indicator: Signs of wound infection under dressing (fever, increased pain, spreading redness)
red_flags.followup_question: Does the wound look infected or do you have a fever?

red_flags.indicator: Uncomplicated dressing change - CTAS Level 5 case example
red_flags.followup_question: Is this a routine dressing change with no other issues?

red_flags.indicator: None - typically non-urgent unless symptomatic
red_flags.followup_question: Are you having any symptoms yourself, or just concerned about exposure?

ctas_level_guidance.5: Exposure to communicable diseases is a single-level complaint (Selected Special Complaints table).

red_flags.indicator: Immunocompromised (neutropenia/suspected, chemotherapy, immunosuppressive drugs)
red_flags.followup_question: Are you currently on chemotherapy, steroids, or any other medication that weakens your immune system?

red_flags.indicator: Looks septic - 3 positive SIRS criteria or hemodynamic compromise/moderate resp distress/altered LOC
red_flags.followup_question: Along with the fever, do you feel very unwell, confused, or short of breath?

red_flags.indicator: Looks unwell - 1-2 positive SIRS criteria, flushed/lethargic/anxious/agitated
red_flags.followup_question: Do you look and feel quite unwell with the fever, even if not extremely so?

red_flags.indicator: Looks well - fever is the only finding, comfortable, no distress
red_flags.followup_question: Aside from the fever itself, do you feel comfortable and not in distress?

red_flags.indicator: Blood glucose >18mmol/L with dyspnea, dehydration, tachypnea, thirst, polyuria, weakness (DKA/HHS pattern)
red_flags.followup_question: Do you know your blood sugar reading, and are you feeling short of breath, very thirsty, or weak?

red_flags.indicator: Blood glucose >18mmol/L, no symptoms
red_flags.followup_question: Is your blood sugar high but you otherwise feel okay?

red_flags.indicator: Blood glucose <3mmol/L with confusion, diaphoresis, behavioural change, seizure, or acute focal deficits
red_flags.followup_question: Do you know your blood sugar reading, and are you feeling confused, sweaty, or shaky?

red_flags.indicator: Blood glucose <3mmol/L, no symptoms
red_flags.followup_question: Is your blood sugar low but you feel otherwise fine?

red_flags.indicator: None - scheduled imaging visit is non-urgent by nature
red_flags.followup_question: Is this a scheduled imaging appointment, and do you have any new symptoms today?

ctas_level_guidance.5: Imaging tests is a single-level complaint (Selected Special Complaints table); also given as a CEDIS example (patient returning to ED for MRI test).

red_flags.indicator: Device malfunction causing acute physiologic compromise (e.g. blocked catheter with respiratory/hemodynamic effect)
red_flags.followup_question: Is the device malfunction causing you breathing trouble, severe pain, or feeling unwell?

red_flags.indicator: Malfunction without acute compromise
red_flags.followup_question: Are you otherwise feeling well despite the device problem?

red_flags.indicator: Any distress or vital sign abnormality on critical look
red_flags.followup_question: Are you in any distress or discomfort right now?

red_flags.indicator: No distress, stable
red_flags.followup_question: Would you say this is a minor issue without significant discomfort?

red_flags.indicator: Hemodynamic compromise or shock (severe anemia/active bleeding)
red_flags.followup_question: Do you feel faint, dizzy, or very weak along with looking pale?

red_flags.indicator: Stable vital signs, known chronic anemia
red_flags.followup_question: Is this a known, longstanding anemia without new symptoms?

red_flags.indicator: Hemodynamic compromise, severe pain, wound dehiscence with evisceration, or signs of sepsis
red_flags.followup_question: Are you feeling faint or very unwell, or has the surgical wound opened up?

red_flags.indicator: Fever or moderate pain, stable vitals
red_flags.followup_question: Do you have a fever, and how severe is the pain at the surgical site?

red_flags.indicator: Mild symptoms, stable
red_flags.followup_question: Are your symptoms mild and manageable?

red_flags.indicator: Symptoms of a medication-related emergency (e.g. missed critical medication causing acute illness)
red_flags.followup_question: Are you experiencing any symptoms from missing this medication?

red_flags.indicator: Routine refill request, no acute symptoms - CTAS Level 5 example
red_flags.followup_question: Is this a routine refill without any new symptoms?

ctas_level_guidance.5: Medication request (CTAS Level 5 example in manual).

red_flags.indicator: Significant swelling with neurovascular compromise of the finger
red_flags.followup_question: Is the finger numb, discolored, or losing circulation because of the ring?

red_flags.indicator: Mild swelling, no neurovascular compromise
red_flags.followup_question: Is the finger otherwise normal in color and sensation?
